claim: The current MCP revision is 2026-07-28. Every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion in _meta; Streamable HTTP also requires MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, and Mcp-Name for named methods. server/discover is a mandatory server RPC and an optional client probe.

Spec compatibility matrix: a legacy (initialize) client against a modern-only server fails with no fall-forward (stdio: server rejects initialize; HTTP: missing modern headers → 400). Dual-era clients work against a modern-only server only if they probe server/discover (stdio) or send a modern request (HTTP) and treat -32022 / -32020 as modern, not as fall-back-to-initialize. Dual-era × dual-era is the specified interoperability path.

Dual-era stdio clients SHOULD send server/discover first. DiscoverResult or a recognized modern error (UnsupportedProtocolVersionError -32022) means stay modern and do not then send initialize. Any other error or timeout means legacy.
Dual-era HTTP clients MUST attempt a modern POST first. On 400 they inspect the body: a recognized modern JSON-RPC error means stay modern; empty or unrecognized means fall back to initialize.

Claude Code 2026-07-28 client support landed in v2.1.232 (v2 runtime = MCP TypeScript SDK 2.0; local binary 2.1.273). Default stdio first message is initialize (legacy); stdio is probed only if MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto. HTTP probes whether the server supports 2026-07-28 when the v2 runtime is active. Against a 2026-07-28-only server, default stdio (including repo:.mcp.json nlp-mcp) fails; HTTP succeeds if v2 is active and the probe is not skipped. Live handshake of 2.1.273 is UNVERIFIED.

Claude Code feature-flag fetch off (Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry, apps gateway, DISABLE_TELEMETRY, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC) uses the v1 runtime unless MCP_SDK_GENERATION=v2 is set, and skips the 2026 probe unless MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto. Set MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy to skip every probe.

OpenAI Codex CLI 2026-07-28 client support shipped in rust-v0.147.0 / CLI 0.147.0 (published 2026-08-07; PRs 35724 and 35725) and remains in local 0.154.0. Default stdio first message is initialize unless CODEX_MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION=2026-07-28. HTTP is legacy lifecycle by default; features.mcp_2026_07_28 (boolean, default off) enables server/discover first with fallback only when a response establishes the endpoint is legacy-only. Default stdio and HTTP against a 2026-only server fail. Live handshake of 0.154.0 is UNVERIFIED.
Codex hosted Apps has a separate default-off flag codex_apps_mcp_2026_07_28; the app-server tree defaults hosted Apps to Legacy.

xAI grok CLI changelog 1.0.29 (2026-09-11) states MCP server connections no longer fail against modern 2026-07-28 servers; local CLI 1.0.34 is after that. HTTP first request is server/discover (ClientLifecycleMode::Discover with V_2026_07_28), then initialize (2025-11-25) on probe error or timeout; connect-phase failures do not fall back; short startup budgets skip the probe. Stdio first message is initialize only, pinned to 2025-11-25, with no server/discover probe and no documented env to opt stdio into 2026. Public grok mcp add docs still do not name a revision.

grok refuses to probe stdio because probing is unsafe: a late discover versus initialize on the same byte stream cannot rebuild the child; a slow server can answer the abandoned discover after initialize is already on the stream, and rmcp then rejects the late response as uncorrelated. Source comment: modern-only stdio servers stay unsupported until rmcp tolerates late responses to abandoned requests. This is a hard G4 blocker for grok-launched stdio hosts including nlp-mcp .mcp.json.

MCP Inspector v2.0.0 (released 2026-07-28, 7aebf16) is the first Inspector line on MCP TS SDK v2; current npm is 2.7.0 (Node >=22.19.0). Default protocolEra is legacy: plain initialize, no probe, because a debugger must not auto-probe (stalls silent stdio; pollutes the transcript). auto = server/discover then fall back. modern = pin 2026-07-28, no fallback. Default fails against a 2026-only server; auto succeeds if the server answers server/discover; modern succeeds on 2026-only and fails loudly on 2025-only.

Official TypeScript SDK @modelcontextprotocol/client v2 first beta 2.0.0-beta.1 (2026-06-30); stable 2.0.0 tagged 2026-07-27. Default versionNegotiation is legacy: initialize, no probe. mode auto probes server/discover (on stdio via a sibling process, because some servers including rmcp exit on pre-initialize requests); the caller's child never sees server/discover. mode pin 2026-07-28 never falls back. Docs warn: do not default a spawn-per-invocation CLI to auto (full probe timeout plus extra process). Default client against a 2026-only server fails. Opaque CORS TypeError during the HTTP probe falls back to legacy; 401/403 are auth, never era; HTTP probe timeout is an outage, not legacy.

Official Python SDK mcp first full client support is 2.0.0b1 (2026-06-30, including stdio auto-mode); GA mcp 2.0.0 on 2026-07-28; current PyPI 2.2.0 (2026-09-07). pip install mcp installs 2.x. Default mode=auto: first message is server/discover at the newest modern version, then initialize if the probe is not positive modern evidence. mode=legacy is initialize only. mode=2026-07-28 is pin with no probe and no handshake (server_info is None unless prior_discover=). Default auto succeeds against a 2026-only server if server/discover returns a DiscoverResult whose supportedVersions includes a modern version.

Python negotiate_auto treats -32022 with a modern-only supported list as a hard incompatibility (raises). -32022 without parseable supported is try initialize, then raise. Any other MCPError on discover falls back to initialize. A client that never reaches server/discover, or whose discover probe is classified as a generic RPC error, will not learn that 2026-07-28 is available from an initialize error body that lacks data.supported.

Official clients disagree on the default handshake. Python SDK v2 Client() and Go SDK Client.Connect send server/discover first. TypeScript SDK v2 new Client() defaults to initialize. C# SDK 2.0 preview notes server/discover then fallback. Claude Code v2 stdio, Codex default, and grok stdio all send initialize; grok stdio has no modern path.

Dual-era is the specified server shape, not a beep invention. The spec dual-era server selects behavior from how the client opens (modern _meta → stateless; initialize → legacy session). Official TS createMcpHandler/serveStdio defaults to serving both eras (legacy: 'stateless'); legacy: 'reject' is the G4 analogue. Python MCPServer answers server/discover on every transport and still accepts handshake-era clients unless the operator forces otherwise. Pinning only v2026_07_28 is the reject setting the reference SDKs expose as a non-default.

A v2026_07_28-only server is exactly the spec Legacy × Modern failure cell for every default-stdio agent that launches in-repo hosts: Claude Code, Codex, and grok all default stdio to initialize. nlp-mcp and the other stdio hosts started from .mcp.json / config.toml therefore break default agent use under G4.

stdio server/discover is load-bearing and easy to get wrong. TS SDK auto on StdioClientTransport probes a sibling process because rmcp-family servers exit on a pre-initialize request. grok refuses in-place stdio probe for the same rmcp late-response reason. mcp-z CLI documents a 60s timeout before fallback when a legacy stdio server never answers an unknown pre-initialize request. TS SDK explicitly: do not default a spawn-per-invocation CLI to auto.

A G4-only stdio server that does implement server/discover is still unreachable from grok (no stdio modern path), from Claude Code without MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto, and from Codex without CODEX_MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION=2026-07-28.

Official conformance server-stateless requires removed RPCs including initialize, ping, logging/setLevel, resources/subscribe, and resources/unsubscribe MUST yield HTTP 404 and JSON-RPC -32601 Method not found (check sep-2575-http-server-method-not-found-404-initialize). Spec versioning says a modern-only server SHOULD name supported versions on any initialize error and that the JSON-RPC code is implementation-defined. A G4 Effect HTTP server that answers initialize as HTTP 400/-32020 HeaderMismatch (or stdio -32022 without data.supported) fails that check until the wire matches 404/-32601 or the suite is waived. Dual-era mixed list would answer initialize successfully and fail the same check for the opposite reason. Conformance --requirements 2026-07-28 is a modern-only referee, not a dual-era referee.

C# SDK 2.0 preview never treats -32022, -32021, or -32020 as legacy indicators. Python auto treats -32022 with modern-only supported as hard incompatibility and -32022 without supported as try initialize then raise. Clients that disagree on whether those codes mean modern versus fallback will split against the same G4 error body.

HTTP 400 is era-ambiguous unless the body is a recognized modern error. A spec-compliant dual-era HTTP client that sees HTTP 400 with -32020 HeaderMismatch (MCP-Protocol-Version header is required) MUST stay modern and not send initialize. A client that treats any 400 as legacy will then send initialize and fail again against a modern-only endpoint.

2026 Streamable HTTP requires Mcp-Method on all requests and Mcp-Name for tools/call, resources/read, and prompts/get. TS SDK notes deployed 2025 servers commonly have CORS allow-lists that predate those headers, so an opaque CORS TypeError during the probe falls back to legacy. Inspector web client skips Mcp-Param-* mirroring in-browser; CLI/TUI on Node mirror correctly. A browser Inspector or TS client on 2026 fails preflight against a host whose CORS omits mcp-method/mcp-name even if G4 handshake is otherwise correct.

Claude Code v2: a channel server that negotiates 2026-07-28 cannot deliver channel messages, so Claude Code does not register it as a channel. Leaving MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION unset keeps stdio on the earlier handshake.
2026 Streamable HTTP removes the GET notification stream; servers SHOULD answer GET/DELETE with 405. Clients that still open GET SSE against a 2026-only server fail at the opening GET.

Community hard-cut pattern: Laravel MCP 1.0 (2026-09-15/16) advertises 2026-07-28; leftover initialize clients get -32601 and must upgrade the client before the server (X @does_it_code, 2026-09-16). Effect G4 initialize error is -32022 rather than -32601, but the operational advice is the same.

Codex stdio 2026 was a filed gap (openai/codex#33952, 18 Jul 2026) asking for 2026-only stdio without initialize; the 28 Jul PR answered with opt-in, not default. Windows Codex + Python stdio initialize response never arriving (openai/codex#29247, Jun 2026) is a 2025-era transport bug that remains relevant because default Codex stdio is still initialize.

Inspector versionNegotiation pin 2026-07-28 throws against a legacy test server; auto falls back (inspector#1700). Inspector tools/call omitted Mcp-Param-* (SEP-2243, inspector#1846, closed by PR #1847, milestone v2.1.0); GitHub MCP rejected with -32020 HeaderMismatch missing Mcp-Param-owner. The web client still skips mirroring in-browser as of 2026-09-16 protocol-eras docs; CLI/TUI on Node are the strict-server path. Current npm 2.7.0 is after v2.1.0 so CLI/TUI should include the fix — UNVERIFIED against a live 2.7.0 process.

Official @modelcontextprotocol/conformance freezes 2026-07-28 in the 0.2.0-alpha.x line (anchor @modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.10, 2026-07-27, per requirements/2026-07-28.yaml). Stable 0.1.16 only speaks through 2025-11-25. The README still shows GitHub Action modelcontextprotocol/conformance@v0.1.11 — UNVERIFIED whether that Action tag accepts --requirements 2026-07-28. Prefer the npx CLI from the 0.2.0-alpha line for a G4 proof. Default without --requirements is everything today, which is not a revision claim. Dated revisions through 2025-11-25 use the stateful lifecycle; 2026-07-28 uses the stateless lifecycle.

conformance server is HTTP-only: the documented invocation is --url; there is no documented --stdio/--command server mode. Stdio beep-effect hosts (nlp-mcp, m365, uspto, gov-legal, practice-kg) cannot be scored by conformance server unless they are also mounted on Streamable HTTP. Client testing uses --command and appends a server URL — that tests a client, not nlp-mcp. Ontology /mcp Origin allowlist plus RPC session token will 403 vanilla conformance server unless a dedicated loopback mount or --expected-failures. SEP-1730 tier-check is for SDKs, optional as a beep-effect host gate.

server-stateless on 2026-07-28 asserts: server/discover MUST exist (supportedVersions + capabilities); missing required _meta → -32602 + HTTP 400; unsupported version → -32022 with data.supported and data.requested + HTTP 400; header/body protocol-version mismatch → -32020 + HTTP 400; removed methods including initialize → HTTP 404 + -32601. Several checks need diagnostic tools (test_missing_capability, test_streaming_elicitation, test_logging_tool) that beep-effect hosts do not register — those report notTestable rather than pass. SEP-2243 http-header-validation is not_scored/pending in the 2026 freeze.

Community HTTP probe mcp-spec-check (npx mcp-spec-check <url>) is black-box HTTP with a YES/NO from three required checks only: discover, routing-headers, session-independence. Warn-only: error codes, cache metadata, MRTR, deprecated features, RFC 9728. No stdio. Useful as a 30-second ontology /mcp smoke after CORS/auth are opened; not a substitute for conformance --requirements 2026-07-28.

Codex scripts/mcp_conformance pins modelcontextprotocol/conformance@49103de6ed70804e940637bf3e9e29e4a3f54e64 and runs it against the Codex executable (legacy + 2025-11-25 + 2026-07-28, HTTP and stdio). That proves Codex-as-client, not beep-effect-as-server. Useful as a recipe for how an agent pins the upstream CLI, not as a G4 proof.

Inspector --cli --protocol-era modern is a 2026 pin canary against each stdio bin; --protocol-era auto proves dual-era; --protocol-era legacy must fail under G4 and must pass under mixed list — that single negative test is the G4 decision distilled. Inspector is not the frozen 2026-07-28 requirement YAML. Exact CLI spelling --protocol-era on Inspector 2.7.0 is UNVERIFIED (TUI source names it; npm README does not restate the default). Python uv run mcp dev is Inspector-backed and does not replace conformance server.

UNVERIFIED in this lane (Gate A finding 25): live stdio/HTTP first-message capture of Claude Code 2.1.273, Codex 0.154.0, and grok 1.0.34 against a 2026-only Effect server. All fail/succeed cells for those three are documented behavior, not a packet capture. Exact JSON-RPC method Claude Code uses for the HTTP newer-revision probe is unnamed in docs. Whether Claude Code v2 stdio with MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto uses the TS SDK sibling-process probe or probes the live child is unread. Whether Codex features.mcp_2026_07_28 alone is enough for HTTP, or CODEX_MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION is also required, is unresolved (PR text ties the env var to stdio). Whether grok CLI 1.0.34 contains the 75810042 handshake code is plausible not proven (source 2026-09-08; npm 1.0.34 on 2026-09-16). Python _probe.py was read from main not the v2.0.0 tag. Official conformance stdio server mode: NOT FOUND in the README.

The spec blog presents 2026-07-28 as the current protocol with no handshake. The TypeScript client default is still the 2025 handshake, with an explicit warning not to flip CLIs to auto. The Python client default is auto. Agent CLIs that wrap rmcp (Codex, grok) kept stdio on initialize because of the late-response / extra-process hazards. The spec is stateless is not the same claim as the clients that launch .mcp.json will speak it.

Zuplo compatibility matrix cells verified 2026-07-31 listed only Inspector 2.0.0 and Python SDK 2.0.0 as reaching 2026-07-28, and Claude Code as initialize era. That row is stale for Claude Code HTTP (docs now describe a v2 probe from 2.1.232, as of 2026-09-15) and still accurate for Claude Code stdio default. Zuplo listed TS SDK 2.0.0 as 2025-11-25, which matches the default mode, not capability. Codex was Not published.

Ontology layerHttp /mcp is the HTTP host: Claude Code v2 (default on 2.1.232+ when flags fetch) and grok HTTP will probe; Codex HTTP needs features.mcp_2026_07_28 = true. Codex hosted Apps remains Legacy unless its separate flag is on.
